findings.title: Untrusted Amazon data is executed with eval()
findings.evidence: After json.loads and ast.literal_eval fail, the adapter calls eval(line) on a line read from downloaded Amazon review/metadata files. fetch_data checks only byte count, not a checksum or signature.
findings.impact: Remote code execution during data preparation or training if an attacker can influence the download source, DNS, or proxy.
findings.recommendation: Remove the eval fallback; use a strict parser or ast allow-list. Add SHA-256 verification for downloads.
findings.notes: Removed eval() fallback from _parse_dict_line in amazon.py; added SHA-256 integrity verification to fetch_data.py.

findings.title: Amazon item cap is computed before the split using test interactions
findings.evidence: The adapter computes item_id.value_counts() over all interactions and keeps the top max_items_in_similarity items. The train/valid/test split is created later, so test-period interactions influence which items survive the cap.
findings.impact: Catalogue and popularity selection are contaminated by test data, violating R2 and inflating product metrics.
findings.recommendation: Split first, then cap by train-only popularity, and assert that test interactions never affect the retained item set.
findings.notes: Moved max_items_in_similarity popularity cap from pre-split raw data preparation into adapter.split(), computing popularity strictly over train_df.

findings.title: MIND history backdating and global dedupe leak future clicks
findings.evidence: Every history item from every session is assigned a timestamp before the user's first impression (line 312), including history from later sessions. Global (user_id,item_id) dedupe keep=last then drops or moves later test clicks. P5.3 remains unchecked, and the only leakage test is real_data and excluded from CI.
findings.impact: Future preferences can enter the training positive set; test clicks can disappear. R2 is not demonstrated on real data.
findings.recommendation: Use true session/impression time boundaries, do not backdate post-boundary history, and add a real-data R2 test that checks clicked item/time rather than only pair intersection.
findings.notes: Tracked user_last_ts across sessions; anchored newly discovered history strictly between prev_ts and imp_ts; changed interaction deduplication to keep='first' so earliest clicks are preserved.

findings.title: CONFORMANCE certifies PASS/0 FAIL with false or missing evidence
findings.evidence: R2 is marked PASS while P5.3 is unchecked and the adapter backdates history. R8 claims <5 ms and ~340 MB while generated RESULTS report 87.23 ms p95 and 796.4 MB RSS. R10 links to nonexistent root NOTICE.md/ATTRIBUTION.md and backend/tests/contract/test_licensing.py. The summary says 0 FAIL.
findings.impact: The primary conformance document gives false assurance about leakage, performance, and licensing evidence.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate from verified evidence, mark R2/P5.3 partial or fail, use generated R8 numbers, fix R10 links, and add the missing licensing test or remove the citation.
findings.notes: Aligned docs/CONFORMANCE.md with pipeline evidence: updated R8 with verified measured numbers (max p95: 87.23 ms, peak RSS: 796.4 MB) matching RESULTS.md, corrected R10 links to backend/discovery/NOTICE.md, docs/ATTRIBUTION.md, and test_vendored_manifest.py, and updated R11 to hmac.compare_digest.

findings.title: Product interactions omit the required positive field
findings.evidence: Interaction.positive is required. MovieLens and MIND set it; Amazon rows contain only user_id, item_id, signal, timestamp. The products parquet has no positive column, and validation silently falls back to signal >= threshold.
findings.impact: Cross-type schema inconsistency; consumers and tuning paths treat products differently from movies/articles.
findings.recommendation: Set positive = signal >= positive_threshold in the Amazon adapter and assert the unified artifact schema across types.
findings.notes: Blocked on Author Decision Q2: Is missing positive column intentional (derive from signal) or an oversight?

findings.title: Tuning scores threshold trials against fixed positive labels
findings.evidence: The candidate spec threshold is changed, but when a positive column exists the code selects valid_df[valid_df['positive'] == True]. MovieLens positive labels were computed once at the original threshold, so 3.5 trials are scored against 4.0 labels.
findings.impact: The threshold dimension of the movie grid search is invalid; the selected threshold may be wrong.
findings.recommendation: Always derive validation positives from signal >= trial threshold, or recompute labels per candidate.
findings.notes: Derived validation positives directly from valid_df['signal'] >= candidate_spec.signal.positive_threshold when signal column exists, ensuring threshold grid trials evaluate against candidate threshold.

findings.title: Articles impression evaluation falls back to all impressions, including train
findings.evidence: If no impression timestamp is greater than train_max_ts, test_impressions is set to the full impressions list.
findings.impact: A short or poorly split dataset evaluates the model on training impressions, inflating AUC/MRR/nDCG silently.
findings.recommendation: Fail or warn prominently when there are no post-train impressions; never evaluate on train impressions.
findings.notes: Removed silent fallback to full impressions list; raised explicit ValueError and logged error when no post-train impressions are found.

findings.title: Articles Random baseline uses process-randomized built-in hash()
findings.evidence: The Random baseline scores with int(abs(hash(ctx))) % 10000000. Three fresh processes produced 5076166, 6895007, and 6011368 for the same context. RandomModel already uses SHA-256.
findings.impact: Articles Random baseline and derived metrics change across processes, weakening P5.8 and P6.3.
findings.recommendation: Use RandomModel or hashlib.sha256(ctx.encode()).digest() for deterministic scoring.
findings.notes: Replaced Python process-randomized hash() with hashlib.sha256(ctx).hexdigest() to guarantee deterministic pseudo-random scoring.

findings.title: Articles cold-start curve is not protocol-identical to the shared harness
findings.evidence: The harness passes exclude_ids built from full training history. The articles loop passes only history and k, and catches every exception from recommend_history and continues, silently dropping failed users.
findings.impact: Articles cold-start metrics use a different candidate set from movies/products and omit failures, so cross-type curves are not comparable.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the harness cold-start loop or pass the same full-history exclusions, and count failures explicitly.
findings.notes: Passed exclude_ids constructed from training history when allow_repeat is False, evaluated metrics against cs_users subset rather than full test set, and logged user failures explicitly.

findings.title: Serving config reconstruction ignores tuned similarity_type and timedecay_formula
findings.evidence: Training writes five tuned parameters, but resolve_serving_config re-applies only top_neighbors_per_item, time_decay_coefficient, and positive_threshold. The broad except at 175-176 hides malformed tuning data. A modified mini artifact with best_params.similarity_type=lift still resolved to jaccard.
findings.impact: A non-default tuned model can fail the manifest hash check at startup (type unavailable) or be served with the wrong configuration.
findings.recommendation: Apply similarity_type and timedecay_formula, and fail loudly on malformed tuning.json.
findings.notes: Reconstructed tuned similarity_type and timedecay_formula to achieve complete parity with train.py; replaced bare exception suppression with explicit ConfigError on corrupt tuning.json.

findings.title: Artifact save is not atomic
findings.evidence: Parquet and JSON files are written in place; the manifest is written last. There is no staging directory, rename, or rollback.
findings.impact: A crash or full disk can leave mixed old/new files or an old manifest whose checksums no longer match, marking the type unavailable.
findings.recommendation: Write to a temporary sibling directory and atomically swap, or use generation IDs and clean incomplete generations on load.
findings.notes: Staged artifact files into a temporary sibling directory before an atomic directory rename swap with rollback protection, preventing partial corruption on mid-write failures.

findings.title: Dependency versions are not locked
findings.evidence: Dependencies use lower bounds only; no uv.lock/requirements pin exists. .gitignore claims uv.lock and package-lock.json are committed, but neither exists.
findings.impact: Environment and CI results are not reproducible over time; a future transitive release can change behavior or introduce vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Commit a lock file for Python 3.11 and install from it in CI.
findings.notes: Generating uv.lock requires external network access to resolve dependency indexes (offline uv cache lacks full resolution tree). Marked BLOCKED-ON-HUMAN per Rule 1.8. Exact command for human: `cd backend && uv lock`.

findings.title: CI deselects 42 real_data tests including P5.3 and P6.3 acceptance tests
findings.evidence: CI runs pytest with -m 'not real_data'; collection shows 42/440 deselected. The leakage and determinism files are wholly marked real_data.
findings.impact: The tests that would catch MIND leakage and verify retraining determinism are not enforced on PRs.
findings.recommendation: Add a scheduled/required real-data job, or run the leakage test on the synthetic fixture in the default job.
findings.notes: Decoupled fixture leakage and determinism tests from real_data marker, ensuring MIND split leakage verification and pipeline determinism run in the default CI suite without requiring external datasets.

findings.title: Search total_matches is capped by limit
findings.evidence: index.search(query, limit) truncates results, then total_matches=len(results). Query q=a has 59 matches but limit=1 returns total_matches=1; limit=5 returns 5. The test only asserts total_matches >= len(results).
findings.impact: Clients cannot know the true match count or implement pagination; the schema field is semantically wrong.
findings.recommendation: Return a separate total count before truncation and test independence from limit.
findings.notes: ItemSearchIndex.search now calculates and returns pre-limit total matches across all ranking tiers; SearchResponse total_matches is independent of limit.

findings.title: Articles metrics hardcode leakage_check_passed: true
findings.evidence: The sanity_checks payload sets leakage_check_passed: True unconditionally; no R2 check is called in this function.
findings.impact: artifacts/articles/metrics.json and /v1/metrics assert a leakage check that never ran.
findings.recommendation: Run the real split leakage check and store its result; fail the pipeline on leakage.
findings.notes: Invoked check_r2_no_leakage(train_df, test_df, strategy) inside run_articles_dual_protocol_eval, failing the evaluation pipeline on leakage.

findings.title: DATASETS production MIND command points to a nonexistent script
findings.evidence: The doc says python backend/scripts/train.py --type articles, but backend/scripts/train.py does not exist. The supported command is cd backend && python -m engine.train --type articles.
findings.impact: A user following the production switch instruction gets a file-not-found error.
findings.recommendation: Replace with the module command or a Makefile target.
findings.notes: Corrected articles training command in docs/DATASETS.md to cd backend && python -m engine.train --type articles (or make train TYPE=articles).

findings.title: ARCHITECTURE claims interactions are split-flagged
findings.evidence: The artifact interactions.parquet has no split/partition column for any type (movies/products/articles); the split is recomputed at evaluation time.
findings.impact: Misleading artifact documentation; users cannot filter train/test from the parquet as described.
findings.recommendation: Either add a split flag to the artifact or correct the description.
findings.notes: Clarified in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md that interactions.parquet stores canonical interactions and train/test splits are dynamically derived via adapter split strategies.

findings.title: Manifest verification joins unvalidated relative paths
findings.evidence: file_path = artifact_dir / rel_path is used for every manifest key without rejecting absolute paths or .. segments.
findings.impact: A tampered manifest can make verification hash files outside the artifact directory. Read-only and requires tampering, so impact is limited.
findings.recommendation: Reject absolute paths and assert each resolved path is contained by artifact_dir.
findings.notes: Enforced path containment in verify_artifacts() by rejecting absolute paths, parent directory traversal (..), and paths resolving outside artifact directory.

findings.title: Item detail reaches into ItemSearchIndex._entries
findings.evidence: The route linearly scans search_indexes[type]._entries to find popularity_rank.
findings.impact: Brittle coupling to a private field and an O(n) scan per item-detail request.
findings.recommendation: Expose a public lookup method or dictionary.
findings.notes: Exposed public get_popularity_rank(item_id) and get_entry(item_id) O(1) lookups on ItemSearchIndex, eliminating private _entries coupling and linear scans.

findings.title: Runtime asserts in library code disappear under python -O
findings.evidence: Bare asserts guard fitted/state invariants in production modules.
findings.impact: Under -O the checks vanish and failures surface later as AttributeError.
findings.recommendation: Raise explicit RuntimeError/ArtifactError in non-test code.
findings.notes: Replaced bare asserts in Amazon adapter, MIND adapter, and TF-IDF recommender with explicit RuntimeError checks that persist under python -O.
